title: Initial unary program semantics
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word and $q\in\mathbb{Q}$. Assume that $q=0$ whenever there are no natural numbers $n,s,t$ such that $x$ has the prescribed unary graph encoding with endpoints $s,t$ and symmetric encoded edge relation. Assume also that for every such encoding with symmetric edge relation, $q$ equals the probability that a uniformly chosen sequence of $100n^4$ edge slots, followed from $s$ in the associated padded regular multigraph, visits $t$. Then the fixed program, started at its initial state with all fifteen registers zero on input $x$, terminates for every sequence of random choices, keeps every register at most $200(|x|+1)^4$, and accepts with probability $q$.

Let $x$ be a bit string and $q$ a rational number. Suppose that $q=0$ whenever there are
no natural numbers $n,s,t$ for which $x$ has the prescribed unary graph encoding with
endpoints $s,t$ and its encoded edge relation is symmetric. Suppose also that, for every
